findings.summary: Some product drawings read as the wrong object or lose their defining part. The leather key ring becomes a magnifying glass (sample 3), a hand holding a fob (sample 2) or a tag with a hand (sample 1). The merino sweater on its detail page is a folded slab held from below that reads as a wallet or card (sample 3). The tote and tea towels have a hand cut off by the plate edge. The reference's small objects read at once.

On the mobile header of the landing holdout, the 'Sign up' button is shorter than the 'Menu' button next to it (tops and bottoms 6px apart). The measured defect is real and shows on every mobile route. The reference does not set two different-height buttons side by side.

The drawing beside the page title on detail pages is sometimes not the page's own subject. The tote's detail page and the sweater's detail page both show a spool in the title slot, next to a large plate of the real object. Seen in two commerce samples.

Small structural variance between samples of one app: the dashboard sidebar has icons in two samples and none in the third; the settings notifications cards are narrow (about 600px) in one sample and full width in the others; the blog newsletter block is left-aligned, split into two columns, or centred with a drawing, depending on the sample.
On the long-form post page the lead stage ends short of the prose column's right edge, and one section heading wraps early with a short first line.

The commerce plates fill the card edge to edge in one sample and sit inset with a margin in the others; the hand that holds the tote and the towels runs off the top edge of the plate in all three, which reads as cropped rather than entering from a side.

notes: Update goal (every card grid of subject items gets a plate, even when the data has no image field): reached in all 3 samples. Blog home has a plate on all 6 posts and the related-post grids carry plates (blog home-desktop-light, posts-release-notes-people-read in each sample); the store grid has a plate on all 11 products in each sample (commerce home-desktop-light). The landing customer grid also has plates on all 8 cards. Link lists, settings groups and the docs browse cards stay text-only, which is right. The rc.2 major does not recur.

Compared with published 1.0.0: no regression found. Listing plates are present as in 1.0.0; metric cards sit 2x2 at 390px (dashboard home-mobile-light, samples 1 and 2); information figures are ghosted previews shaped like their captions (blog posts-shipping-a-design-system, posts-release-notes-people-read).

Earlier verdicts: rc.2's major (lost listing plates) is fixed. critic-1's minors (key ring, sweater, lead stage width) still appear and are listed once above. Invoice badges that stretched on mobile in critic-1 hug their text in the sample I opened (settings billing-mobile-light, sample 2); not re-raised.

Measured defect, false alarm: repeated-drawing on blog /posts/release-notes-people-read (desktop and mobile, 2 samples). The repeated SVG is svg.stage-lines, the faint wandering-line texture the spec puts on every stage (lead stage and figure stage), not an illustration shown twice. The reference's media stage has the same line texture (p1-desktop-light).
Measured defect, confirmed as minor: landing mobile 'Sign up' next to 'Menu', 6px mismatch on all four mobile routes (signup-mobile-light).

Capture artifacts, not counted: the sidebar rule ends at the 900px viewport height and the dialog scrim ends mid-page in full-page captures (settings state-plan-dialog-mobile-light); the header-in motion frames show a stage under the fixed header because of the full-page capture.

Opened: all 3 samples of blog, commerce, dashboard and settings (home or first route at desktop light, plus mobile, dark, detail routes and state captures, including focus, error, empty, dialog, user menu, search-empty, added-to-cart and checkout errors, across samples); the landing holdout (home, pricing, customers, signup, mobile, dark) and the docs holdout (home, a doc page, changelog); drawing crops (commerce key ring, blog featured fan) against reference p3-i1 and the reference screenshot; motion strips (blog hero cel-run and header-in).

Motion: the hero hand-and-pen draws cel by cel with the colour fill then the hand entering from the right edge, and holds (blog motion-m1), the same behaviour as the spec asks. Not seen: loops or anything that ignores reduced motion.

Holdouts: the landing page carries the system (serif display, cream paper, sage hero stage with a ghosted product preview, line drawings over feature headings, pricing plans on a sage stage, ink footer). The docs page keeps its prose calm with one header drawing, tabs, code blocks with Copy, designed callouts in three tones and a typed changelog with badges. A text-first docs page without plates is right. No blocker or major in either.
Gates passed on all apps; the smoke tests were not run for this screen, as the brief says.
